audit.whatIsWrong: The whole full layer tracks an ability called 'Repeating Dashes'. Ambessa has no such ability. It appears in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, four phase whys, five breakdown fields, the do's and six report entries. Nothing anywhere named Repudiation's shield or grounding.
audit.why: Ambessa's real kit is Drakehound's Step (P, the dash that fires off any ability cast, with an empowered next attack), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q, 14/13/12/11/10s), Repudiation (W, 18/17/16/15/14s — shield, brace, grounding), Lacerate (E, 13/12/11/10/9s) and Public Execution (R, 130/115/100s — blink, suppress, stun). Repudiation grounding is the decisive interaction: Hop (E, 22s at rank 1) is Gnar's only escape and grounding removes it, so the trade cannot be exited once she braces.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced with the real abilities; the tracked cooldown is now Repudiation (18s) and the grounding-versus-Hop interaction is stated in the cooldown block, do's, report and the level-3 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage of the chart contradicted its own why. whys[0] says Gnar wins level 1 while win[0] said Skill; whys[1] calls level 2 a coinflip while win[1] said Gnar; whys[2] through whys[5] describe Ambessa owning 3 onward while the chart gave those to Gnar or Skill.
audit.why: The prose is right and matches the kit: no dash chain at 1, Drakehound's Step chaining from 3 onward, her bruiser item weaving around a telegraphed Wallop line. Gnar also loses the matchup at 49.29%.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Gnar, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill — identical to the packet chart and to the existing whys.

audit.why: Spike text already handles the point most Gnar pages get wrong: GNAR! arrives with the Mega transform, not at level 6, so 6 is not a Gnar spike. Ambessa's spikes are 3 (dash chain), 6 (Public Execution, 130s at rank 1) and first item.
audit.corrected: Kept; breakdown.spikes now names Drakehound's Step instead of the fabricated ability.

notes: 'Repeating Dashes' is fabricated and was the tracked ability across the entire full layer; I replaced it everywhere on a writable path. It may also survive in non-writable fields on this matchup (and WKM_LINES is champion-level and out of scope), so a grep for 'Repeating Dashes' after the applier runs is worth doing. Level-chart flips are proposed as one atomic group across both layers and land on the packet chart, which the existing whys already described. I asserted nothing about whether Public Execution's suppression can be cleansed or QSS'd — Riot's text does not say and the kit's needsResearch is empty by design.
